info.title: Patient Contact regional event publishers
info.description: Unreleased documentation-only proposal for the patient service publishing boundary, including API audit producer and transactional-outbox relay. Operations are from this publisher application perspective. Workers are separate receiving applications; their own operations/queue mappings must be qualified, not inferred by flipping send to receive. Event payloads proposed as v1/1.0.0 are not released contracts. See ../docs/events.md.

regionalSqs.description: Illustrative commercial-AWS regional SQS endpoint, accessed using TLS/SigV4 and IAM workload identity. Region/cell/account ownership is backend controlled; AWS China requires separate deployment qualification. Defaults are synthetic examples, not selected launch placement.

region.description: Qualified AWS deployment region, never chosen by event input.

x-aws-authentication.authorization: least-privilege queue and KMS policies; separate domain and audit roles

domainEvents.description: One regional cell/environment queue with competing replicas of one domain-worker application; independent subscribers require distinct queues/fanout.
domainEvents.x-address-resolution: Logical queue name; deployment inventory resolves the actual account, cell, environment, queue URL/ARN, KMS key and DLQ. No cloud resource is created by this document.

auditIntents.description: Separate restricted regional audit queue; durable acceptance is required before disclosure. Audit archive worker is independently authorized.
auditIntents.x-address-resolution: Logical queue name; deployment inventory resolves the actual account, cell, environment, queue URL/ARN, KMS key and DLQ. No cloud resource is created by this document.

publishDomainEvents.title: Durable outbox relay publishes committed domain events
publishDomainEvents.x-delivery-semantics: at-least-once; duplicates and out-of-order delivery possible
publishDomainEvents.x-authorization: AWS SigV4 using a scoped workload identity and queue/KMS policies. No end-user JWT is placed in a message.
publishDomainEvents.description: Send only immutable events from committed regional outbox/publication evidence. Preserve identity/content across attempts; receivers require provenance, tenant/workflow binding and current effect/retention/recovery fences. A successful send is transport acceptance, not business or erasure completion.

publishDisclosureIntent.title: API durably publishes authorized disclosure intent before returning protected data
publishDisclosureIntent.x-delivery-semantics: at-least-once; duplicates and out-of-order delivery possible
publishDisclosureIntent.x-authorization: AWS SigV4 using a scoped workload identity and queue/KMS policies. No end-user JWT is placed in a message.
publishDisclosureIntent.description: Publish the exact frozen authorized disclosure intent through the separate audit producer role. Await durable acceptance, then revalidate freshness/deadline/erasure fences before response bytes. Changed projection uses a new event identity or aborts. This operation does not add a per-read patient-database outbox.

retentionDecisionGeneration.description: Authoritative monotonic retention/legal-hold decision generation for this erasure workflow. A superseded generation cannot authorize destructive work or completion; current workflow/participant fences still must be checked. This is not a permission grant or the deletion generation.

ErasureCompletedData.description: Emitted only after verified workflow completion under the recorded retention-decision generation, including backup/restore and registered-copy obligations. Current authenticated participant evidence and recovery fences are required. Never emitted for 202 acceptance, active_data_erased, queue acceptance, stale evidence or unresolved retention.

AuditDisclosureReference.description: Exact disclosed field categories for one patient, including authorized container metadata; contains no values or principal-bound ETag.

DisclosureIntentData.description: Restricted intent derived from the exact frozen authorized response projection; not proof of browser receipt. After durable acknowledgment, revalidate freshness/deadline and erasure/disclosure fences before response bytes. A changed projection requires abort or a new event identity. Empty disclosures is valid for an authorized no-match lookup. No token, raw claims, search value, contact data or free text.

x-validation-status: JSON/reference/example and used-schema-keyword consistency checks only. Normative security extensions require application/transport conformance tests. Exact AsyncAPI 3.1.0 parser, general schema validation, renderer and Go generation remain unqualified; no runtime/security conformance claimed.

x-security-invariants.status: proposed; normative application and transport requirements, not enforced by AsyncAPI schema validation alone

producerProvenance.domain: Before dispatch, match source/id/tenantid/patientId/type/dataschema/generations and immutable content to the committed outbox record or protected immutable publication evidence. Retain that evidence for the permitted replay horizon. Verify tenant placement and migration authority independently.
producerProvenance.audit: Only the separately authorized API audit producer may publish disclosure intent. Derive actorRef, tenant, patient references and fields from the validated backend decision and frozen response, never caller-supplied event claims. No per-read DynamoDB outbox is introduced.
producerProvenance.transport: Use TLS/SigV4 with scoped IAM queue/KMS roles. The inner source string or tenantid is not authentication. Validate permitted AWS-service source accounts/ARNs and native-wrapper adapter before trusting a delivery.
producerProvenance.roles: Relay, audit producer, audit archive writer, erasure participant and queue/retention administrator have distinct required capabilities. Ordinary workers cannot purge queues, bulk redrive, change retention/holds, restore/export data or administer keys.

identityAndIntegrity.identity: consumer identity + inner CloudEvents source + id
identityAndIntegrity.content: Persist a digest of the entire inner CloudEvent under a qualified versioned canonical-JSON serialization. Include tenant/type/schema/data; exclude native broker delivery metadata. Immutable producer evidence uses the same content comparison.
identityAndIntegrity.identicalRedelivery: Same identity and identical content is an idempotent duplicate.
identityAndIntegrity.conflictingRedelivery: Same identity and different content is an integrity failure: quarantine/alert without overwriting prior evidence or silently accepting it as processed.
identityAndIntegrity.authority: A digest comparison detects conflicting content against protected evidence; it does not authenticate an untrusted publisher.

consumerEffects.atomicity: Persist inbox and local effect or durable work intent together, conditioned on current record/restriction/deletion fences. A prior strong read alone is insufficient.
consumerEffects.externalEffects: External destinations enforce idempotency and generation fences. Erasure participants close admission, fence, drain/cancel in-flight work, purge and verify before acknowledging completion.
consumerEffects.restriction: Late ordinary updates cannot lower access generation or undo current restrictions; events are not permission grants.
consumerEffects.erasure: Terminal tombstones dominate replay, and erased patient IDs are not reused. The erasure-start message is an approved workflow fact, not unconditional purge authority.

retentionAndCompletion.decisionFence: Destructive admission/effects require the current authoritative retentionDecisionGeneration, workflow state, approved action, registered participant and work fence. Newly accepted holds advance the decision generation and invalidate outstanding destructive admission.
retentionAndCompletion.staleStart: A superseded start decision cannot authorize purge. Preserve/reconcile the workflow; resumption requires an explicit authorized transition and new immutable event identity with the current decision generation, not mutation of the old event.
retentionAndCompletion.completionEvidence: Callbacks are authenticated and bound to tenant/patient/request, deletion and retention-decision generations, registered participant, work attempt and recovery epoch. Stale evidence cannot advance completion.
retentionAndCompletion.completionMeaning: completed includes all defined backup/restore and registered-copy obligations; active_data_erased, queue acceptance, stale callbacks and unresolved retention are insufficient.
retentionAndCompletion.holdRace: Serialize hold changes with deletion admission. Bound in-flight destructive units and report deletion already committed before a hold accurately; no retroactive undo is promised.

auditDisclosure.freeze: Freeze the response projection and exact audit references/revisions/field categories/policy version together.
auditDisclosure.revalidate: After durable acknowledgment and before response bytes, recheck authorization freshness, deadline and erasure/disclosure fences. Do not enlarge or substitute the accepted projection.
auditDisclosure.changedProjection: Abort or issue a newly authorized projection with a new audit event identity within the deadline; never mutate/reuse an accepted intent identity.
auditDisclosure.meaning: An accepted intent may outlive an aborted response and is not proof of browser receipt.
auditDisclosure.archive: Append idempotently with integrity evidence; separate append from archive-administration/deletion rights and protect privileged access logs.

recoveryAndReplay.epoch: Restore/rebuild starts a fenced recovery epoch. Reconcile actual data, inbox state, participant receipts and the protected current erasure ledger before readiness.
recoveryAndReplay.oldEvidence: An old processed inbox record or receipt does not prove a restored copy is erased; re-establish local effects/fences and reject former-epoch callbacks.
recoveryAndReplay.retention: Minimize and classify inboxes, provenance, tombstones, queues/DLQs and archives as restricted linkable data with approved retention/replay horizons.
recoveryAndReplay.redrive: Authorized bounded redrive preserves identity/content, re-runs provenance/schema/fence checks, and never changes residency or bypasses tombstones.

resourceBounds.required: Enforce reviewed byte/depth/string/array/batch/deadline and retry/work-amplification bounds before expensive processing. Reject duplicate JSON member names and unsupported encodings.
resourceBounds.schemas: Resolve only pinned local/controlled schema identities; no runtime network fetch from event dataschema.
resourceBounds.fairness: Bound tenant/producer/cell work and reserve audit/erasure capacity. Accepted required audits cannot be sampled or silently dropped.
resourceBounds.quarantine: Use restricted regional quarantine/DLQ with bounded retries. Never put rejected event bodies, identifiers or raw parser errors in ordinary logs.
resourceBounds.qualification: Numerical operating budgets remain to be selected and tested against maximum valid messages before implementation acceptance.
